instructions: The app shows a calories-today tracker. Call a tool only when the user wants to log, change, undo or check THEIR OWN calories for today. A question about how many calories a food has is general knowledge: answer it directly, without any tool. Only use the tools listed below; for anything else answer normally. A tool result with "ok": true means the change is already made: say in one short sentence what was done; never ask whether to do it. Never offer or suggest logging food unless the user talks about something they ate or drank.
missingToolReply: Sorry, I couldn't update the calorie tracker. Could you say it again, maybe with the number of calories?

rules.comment: "How many calories are in an apple?" is general knowledge
"Remove the kiwi", "I didn't eat the coke" delete that line
Logging, including follow-ups without a verb ("And a banana"); not questions ("How many calories have I had?")

any: \b(how (much|many)( calories)? (have|did) i|my total|so far|today's total|calories (have i|today)|what have i eaten|what did i eat)\b

routing.autoToolsComment: Tools the model may use on its own when no rule picked a tool: reading the tracker only. Changes need the user's words to match a rule.
routing.defaultComment: When no rule matches, the turn has no tools and the model just answers ("Hello, how are you?"). It becomes "auto" when the app, an MCP server or memory adds tools only the model can choose; then autoTools limits this skill to reading.

tools.name: get_calories_today
tools.description: Read the user's calorie tracker: today's total and entries.

tools.name: log_food
tools.description: Log something the user says they ate or drank ('I ate', 'I had', 'log', 'add'). Give the food name and quantity; the app knows the calories of common foods. Set calories only if the user said a number.

food.description: Food or drink, singular, e.g. egg, banana, slice of pizza, can of coke. Use 'calories' if the user only said a number.

calories.description: Total calories, only if the user said the number

tools.name: delete_food
tools.description: Delete a food or drink from today's list ('remove the kiwi', 'delete the coke', 'I didn't eat the banana').

food.description: The food to delete, e.g. kiwi, or 'last' for the last one

tools.name: remove_calories
tools.description: Subtract a number of calories from today's total ('remove 100 calories'). To remove a food, use delete_food.

tools.name: set_calories_today
tools.description: Replace today's total with an exact number, e.g. 'set it to 1500', 'reset to zero', 'today I ate 1200 in total'.

tools.name: undo_last_change
tools.description: Undo the last change to the calorie tracker ('undo', 'that was wrong', 'cancel that').

fillers: I need to check online for the calories in {food}.
{Food} isn't on my list, so let me look it up online.
Let me look up the calories for {food} online.
One moment, I'm checking online how many calories {food} has.
Give me a second to find {food} online.
Let me search online for the calories in {food}.

fallbackArguments.comment: When the model doesn't call log_food after a retry, the food (and count) come from the user's words: these patterns are removed (after the grams), then a leading count is read

strip: \b(?:today|tonight|this morning|please|too|as well|to my list|to the tracker)\b

messages.unknownFood: I couldn't find {food} in my food list{searchedOn}.
messages.askCalories: How many calories did it have?
messages.deleteNotFound: I couldn't find {food} in today's list. The list has: {list}. Which one should I remove?
messages.deleteEmpty: Today's list is empty, so there is nothing to remove.
messages.removeAskAmount: How many calories should I remove?
messages.statusUndone: Done: the last change was undone
